text:
Marathon Petroleum stock has fallen 18.5% over two weeks, with today's decline continuing a sharp selloff that accelerated after the November 3rd midterm elections. The core driver appears to be political: a Democratic sweep in the midterms has shifted market expectations toward stronger support for renewable energy and away from fossil fuels, creating a headwind for oil refiners. This concern has outweighed the company's own quarterly earnings report released the same day, suggesting investors are pricing in a longer-term structural shift in energy policy rather than reacting to near-term financial results.

The refining backdrop provides some support—refineries are running near full capacity at 94.5%, and crude oil remains elevated above $99 per barrel—but these operational positives haven't offset the political overhang. The Democratic Congress now in power represents the opposite of the pro-fossil-fuel stance refiners benefited from under the prior administration, making investors anxious about the sector's multi-year outlook despite solid current margins.
